PullRequest.Title: Add regression coverage for nested chat action alignment
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary
- add a blocking dark/light component fixture for compact nested chat rows that show both a workspace badge and the Mark as Done primary action
- extend the shared Sessions test builder to model multi-folder sessions and chat workspaces with a non-empty folder contract
- verify the existing shared toolbar layout keeps the primary action at the trailing edge

Follow-up to #337915.

## Validation
- `npm run typecheck-client`
- `npx component-explorer render -p test/componentFixtures/component-explorer.json --fixture-id-regex SessionsList_CompactNestedChatPrimaryAction --target /tmp/vscode-archive-action-feedback`

Scenarios.Scenario: Blocking dark/light component screenshot for the compact nested-chat primary-action row
Scenarios.CriticalPath: When the new fixture is selected by component-explorer/CI, each theme constructs one session with one peer chat, renders the production sessions-list DOM through mocked services, applies focus, and waits for the fixture's scheduled settling before screenshot capture. This work is test-only and is not on VS Code product startup or interaction paths.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Fixed at two default theme variants, one session, one peer chat, and two workspace folders. The folder-to-URI/object mapping is linear in the explicitly supplied folder list, here cardinality 2.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each fixture render builds its state synchronously; dark/light variants are independent and runner scheduling is outside this diff. The changed code adds no Promise fan-out, limiter bypass, queue, subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is involved. Fixture definitions retain only small static specs until selected; each selected render creates fresh in-memory test models and DOM, as before for every fixture.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed fixture options, default dark/light expansion, buildTestSession call path, and mocked service setup are directly visible. No external expensive boundary is reached by the changed state construction.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact CI scheduling and screenshot duration are runner-dependent, but the added workload is deliberately bounded to one fixture with two theme variants and tiny fixed data.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Adding bounded regression coverage intentionally adds a small CI-only render and does not alter product runtime performance.

Scenarios.Scenario: Existing unit tests and component fixtures constructing test session workspaces
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A test or selected fixture calls buildTestSession/buildTestChat; workspace creation now maps folder labels into URI and folder objects before returning the in-memory ISessionWorkspace. This completes before the test model can render, but remains test-only.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: For all existing callers that omit workspaceFolders, effective cardinality remains one folder per workspace. New explicit multi-folder specs cost O(folder count); the added fixture uses two. Peer-chat workspaces also remain one folder because they do not pass a folder list.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Workspace and folder construction is synchronous and serial inside each test-model build. No asynchronous work or aggregate concurrency is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: There was no workspace cache before and none is added or defeated. Each builder call creates fresh test URI/folder objects; the default path changes from direct singleton construction to a one-element map with bounded allocation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: repository search shows buildTestWorkspace is defined and called only in the shared test builder, whose consumers are the sessions component fixture and sessions-list tests.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The total number of test fixture invocations varies by selected suite, but repository callers are confined to test/fixture code and the default extra map callback is constant-size.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The change adds a constant, negligible test-only allocation for existing one-folder callers and linear work only when tests explicitly request multiple folders.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over the full two-file diff and traced fixture registration, rendering, builder callers, folder cardinality, theme multiplicity, mocked services, caches, and concurrency. The PR changes only test/component-fixture infrastructure; it introduces no actionable product performance regression and no concrete shipped regression fix requiring blame.
